articleTitle: The effects of moisture on performance of polymeric cables
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: Water, or the excess of it, has always been implicated in poor performance, sometimes to the point of failure, of highly stressed insulation systems as used in cables. This is no less true in the families of extruded polymeric dielectric systems with current and projected use at voltages up to 500 kV. Here, the authors examine the effects of moisture on the performance of polymeric power cables by studying the following cable insulation systems: XLPE; EPR; MDPE/HDPE; and PVC.

articleTitle: Insulations for polymeric supertension cables
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: This paper deals with the types, selection and processing of insulation materials for polymeric cables in the voltage range, 66 to 500 kV. Cables in this voltage class require insulations which provide: physical integrity, dimensional integrity, and electrical integrity. The influence of these requirements on the selection of polymeric insulations (LDPE, HDPE, EPR, XLPE) are discussed.

articleTitle: On-site testing of cable systems after laying, monitoring with HF partial discharge detection
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: At KEMA, a new high frequency measuring technique is developed to detect partial discharges in HV polymer insulated power cables and accessories. This complete system makes it possible to perform on-site PD measurements focused on accessories, without any connection to high voltage parts of the system. The measurements are based on newly developed techniques, while the PD determination is based on traditional rules because of the PD-phase-angle relation. The first field measurements with this complete system are presently being performed.

articleTitle: On-site testing of high voltage cable systems after laying; voltage tests
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: The purpose of on-site tests on HV power cable systems is to detect defects in assembled accessories in new systems and to check the reliability of accessories and cables of systems already being in service. On-site tests should be effective to detect possible defects, but should not cause any damage. Here, attention is focussed on testing of the cable's main insulation by means of DC voltage or oscillating wave voltage or very low frequency voltage or AC voltage 50 Hz or AC voltage with another frequency. The level of the test voltage and major requirements for test equipment are discussed. A view is also given regarding which system will be used in the future.

articleTitle: Supertension (66-500 kV) polymeric cables and their accessories
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: Among the different types of joints the prefabricated designs are nowadays the more extensively used, due to their intrinsic higher reliability, as they are factory moulded and factory routine tested at HV before installation on site. In addition, the prefabricated concept allows a reduction in jointing time and jointing skill which can however differ according to the design and fitting concept. Two main types of prefabricated joints are used: (a) the composite type, and (b) the premoulded type. The composite type joint includes two premoulded rubber stress cones, which are pressed by a spring system against the cable core, and a conically shaped central insulator of cast thermoset resin. The premoulded type joint includes a moulded EPR or silicone rubber one piece or three pieces sleeve, which is (are) interference fitted over the prepared cable core. The author describes these types of joint.

articleTitle: Outer protection for accessories and thermomechanical considerations
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: The author presents a study on outer protection for power cable accessories in which he concludes that there are a number of significant thermo-mechanical defects that are present in XLPE power cables but that all of these can be accommodated fully if they are taken into account in both the power cable and installation design.

articleTitle: Cable and accessory installation
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: This paper emphasises the care necessary to ensure a satisfactory XLPE power cable installation capable of giving a service life at least equal to that of paper cable. Some of the precautions taken during installation and the sophistication of the environment and techniques used may seem more than might be expected, especially compared to the humble low voltage origins of polymeric cable. It is however the case that if you reduce the engineering specification then inevitably you put the service reliability at risk. Such risks become less acceptable as system voltages and conductor sizes rise, because of the reduced factors of safety and the higher electrical and thermomechanical performance requirements.

articleTitle: Core design stress levels
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: The methods for designing the cable insulation thickness of EHV cables are based on the mean or the maximum stress. It mainly consists in determining the design field strengths of the insulation: the AC field strength and the lightning impulse field strength are generally considered. The most complete approach is based on the statistical analysis of the reference strength. Besides the design methods based on fixed values for either maximum or mean stress, the statistical method takes fully into account the volume effect for the insulation breakdown. For a global reliability of the design, constraints or possible limiting factors such as the following are also to be considered: external stress allowed by accessories (field strength at the interface); acceptable AC breakdown risk level in service; and AC voltage level for the routine test. The paper summarizes these methods on the basis of examples taken from published papers and on the report of CIGRE WG 21.04 who had been given the task of assessing the design criteria for HV extruded cables. Current practice for conductor and external stress on EHV cables is also considered.

articleTitle: Supertension polymeric cables and their accessories. Overview of cable engineering. Basic principles: a users view
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: This paper is summarises one user's view with regard to the adoption of 66 and 132 kV polymeric cables (XLPE insulation), the basic engineering requirements associated with choice of design and installation of cables and accessories and subsequent experience. Also, design changes to achieve longer cable lengths for tunnel installations have been consolidated.

articleTitle: Basic principles of accessory design [for polymeric power cables]
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: Accessories are key elements in extruded polymeric cable transmission circuits, being indivisible in importance from the cable itself. They are required to exhibit an equal performance to the cable to achieve the highest system rating at the lowest component and assembly cost. The continued development of the accessories is the determining factor in making possible the application of reliable cable systems particularly at the higher transmission voltages. In this paper, the author discusses insulation design, the classification of accessory types and presents a worldwide survey of such accessories.

articleTitle: Polymeric terminations
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: The positive experiences made over more than 25 years with EHV composite insulators lead to the development of polymeric cable terminations. Polymeric terminations have the following advantages compared to porcelain terminations: low weight, less fragile, better flashover performance, power arc resistance, and higher abrasion resistance (sand storm). The author discusses composite, dry type and heat shrink terminations, and their material requirements, shed design and testing.

articleTitle: Manufacturing technologies and factory test techniques for accessories components
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: Accessories are key elements in cable systems. Development is in progress mainly in the higher voltage field and for prefabricated accessories. This paper gives an insight into the special manufacturing requirements in relation to straight joints and outdoor terminations. To ensure that performance and quality of accessories is achieved, a quality assurance system and representative approval tests are needed.

articleTitle: EPR taped joints and prefabricated composite joints
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: Joints for polymeric insulated supertension cable fall into three main types based on the insulating method employed: (1) fluid or gas immersed, (2) elastomeric, and (3) field moulded. This paper considers two types of elastomeric insulated joints, the EPR (ethylene-propylene rubber) taped joint and the prefabricated composite joint.

articleTitle: Thermo-mechanical Considerations
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension

articleTitle: Statistical treatment of breakdown tests for extruded insulation
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: If identical extruded HV power cables are stressed under identical conditions, they will not breakdown after the same period of time. Consequently it is not possible to predict the life of cable insulation even in the unlikely event of knowing the exact service conditions and knowing the life of a similar cable under similar conditions. It is therefore necessary to consider the lifetimes of cables as following a statistical distribution. This paper considers the statistical nature of breakdown and how applied voltage may influence the lifetime. Some examples are given, but unfortunately very little conclusive data have been published for high voltage cables to date.

articleTitle: European standards for supertension cables. Additional requirements over and above those in IEC840
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: IEC840 was written by IEC Study Committee 20A Working Group 11, based on a recommendation produced by CIGRE SC 21 WG9. The recommendation was the result of international collaboration and agreement and based on surveys of practice in Europe and Japan, supplemented by research and development data provided by the participants. Not all the recommendations were taken on board as IEC's goal is a standard having worldwide acceptance and not just reflecting requirements of utilities in Europe. CENELEC TC20 WG9 has had the task of collating national requirements for a set of compendium approach Harmonised Documents (HDs) for LV and MV cables. The accompanying HDs for accessories on the other hand reflect a rationalisation approach. When it came to writing the HV polymeric cables HD632, the WG decided that this should be achieved in a similar manner, by using IEC840 as a base with a minimum input in the form of additional national requirements. The outcome was unexpected with some 500 pages of text offered as additional national data. This paper examines some additions that are being discussed in international fora and may find their way into HD632 and also those changes to IEC840 that could eventually also form part of HD632. IEC840 covers tests for system voltages higher than 30 kV and up to 150 kV and there are plans to extend this to 500 kV. HD632 covers the same voltage range.

articleTitle: Overview of cable engineering
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: The author briefly summarises the modus operandi of traditional cable systems and then compares them with extruded insulation cable systems. The traditional cables discussed include paper impregnated cables and pressurised cables. The author then discusses the advantages of extruded insulated cables of the traditional designs. The main advantage is the elimination of hydraulic systems. The failure mechanism of extruded insulated cables, due to electrical discharge activity, is also discussed.

articleTitle: Overall design of supertension cables
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: The author describes how, during the design of supertension (66 kV to 500 kV) polymeric power cables, it is necessary to not only consider the electrical performance of the dielectric but also the correct choice of overall cable design to perform a variety of functions. The polymeric insulation must be protected from the surrounding environment by a radial metallic moisture barrier and suitable protection from the forces generated by thermal expansion, installation conditions or accidental damage. In service the core protection will be subjected to: (1) capacitive charging currents; (2) circulating currents; (3) transient fault currents; and (4) transient voltages which all must be designed for and adequately dissipated. The cable design is completed with a polymeric oversheath which can be modified to be abrasion resistant, termite resistant or have enhanced fire performance to suit the particular installation conditions. All of these influences must be considered in the overall design of a supertension polymeric cable.

articleTitle: Overview of accessory engineering. Termination technologies
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: The advent of polymeric power cables quite naturally led to the requirement for compatible accessories. This paper is limited to terminations that follow the conventional fluid filled cable philosophies, adapted for polymeric cables. By the time that polymeric cables were entering the market, fluid filled cable terminations were established in three main categories, viz. outdoor, oil immersed (transformer direct connections) and SF/sub 6/ immersed (GIS or metal clad switchgear direct connections). The CIGRE WG21-06 have produced Publication 89 entitled 'Accessories for HV Extruded cables' 1995. This report covers joints, including transition joints, as well as the termination types mentioned above and a glossary of definitions. The report illustrates typical examples of the various categories within the broad headings. In this paper, the more common types of designs in current use are considered.

articleTitle: The prefabricated CLICK-FIT joint
publicationTitle: IEE Two Day Colloquium on Supertension
abstract: A new generation of accessories for (E)HV polymeric insulated cable systems has been introduced. These accessories take increased benefit of the advantages of polymeric cables when compared to the more conventional oil filled cables. The one-piece CLICK-FIT joint is part of this generation. Due to prefabricated components and simple installation techniques, the reliability of the joint is increased and the total costs of ownership are decreased. Presently the CLICK-FIT principle is in development for other accessories, like terminations. The authors describe the CLICK-FIT joint and its testing and installation.
